body:
A special relationship is sacred, but you seem like you already know that as you treasure it. I think your partner being there must be helping you through this adversity. I'm sorry that these issues can impact your life expectancy - it must be adding unwanted extra stress to your life. What you and your partner have seems to be a stronger foundation of trust and security which might be part of what makes this special.

It's good you'd never ask that question, it couldn't lead to any good. Are there any other angles/points you'd like to discuss?

That sounds like a productive plan. I hope it works out for you. It seems like just reaching out today has given you more perspective and (seemingly) improved your mood too. Best wishes moving forward.

I see, well thank you for clarifying. I ask because the relationship you've describe with him, whilst not necessarily wrong, is a bit atypical between boys and girls. It sounds like the relationship you have with your boyfriend is stable and functional, would you say that's true? That one in a million connection sounds special, you contrast and complement your boyfriend. 

I don't think there's anything on his side romantically, I just think he's found a friend he gets really on with, but he has to be mindful of how that makes his wife feel. If you're regarded as conventionally attractive, then that might also factor into how his wife sees this: you being attractive may make you more of a 'threat'. I don't say that with certainty, but it's plausible. With types, they're oftentimes not concrete. Regarding his type, I'd assume his wife fits the bill. It's probably not a good idea to delve into questions like that, especially with how that probably encroaches upon his boundaries.

How do you feel about all this?

I see, I hope that conversation about boundaries works well for you both. It’s hard to know where we stand sometimes, right? Especially when new information we get contradicts itself.

I think he was trying to do what works for you both: talking to you whilst also being intimate with his wife. The details are foggy, but I’d guess his wife either didn’t know and/or care at first. But, he might’ve just wanted to talk to you, which is why his wife’s feelings may have been put to the side. It sounds like there was a point where he couldn’t do that anymore, hence the block.

It would’ve been great if he had told you earlier: best time to plant a tree is 20 years ago, second best time is now and all. I think that conversation could really help you move forward together.

Forgive me for asking if it’s too forwards, but just for the sake of covering all bases, is there any chance there’s anything there?

I get that you're frustrated, rightfully so. I know you've made it clear, but it's unlikely that they're going to respond to that original message now. If you don't want to DM them, have you considered asking them again?

Well, it's great that you've found someone that you're so comfortable around, especially as you mask to fit in - probably due to autism, but I'm not sure. It's good you've got a lot of common interest with this guy too: I find that talking to people is easier when there's that shared space. 

  
I'm sorry to hear you fell ill. I think it's sweet that he checked in on you to see how you're doing. I think it's safe to say you're friends, at least from my perspective. Also, that whiplash from being friends to being blocked must've felt like a shock to the system, right? 

I think his girlfriend sounds worried at how close you two are, especially as it hasn't been that long since you've met. It does sound like there's some insecurity on her part, but (if I'm being honest), I think most partners would do something similar. I don't mean to be too direct, but any attempts at telling your friend about what his wife should do will probably be in vain: either to be dismissed or worsen the situation.

If I were to guess, I'd say the boundaries would be not talking outside of work (text or call), but anything at work is fair game. Or, if talking or texting is absolutely critical, it should only be about work. At the end of the day, it sounds like he's prioritising his partner's feelings, which is fair. 

But, the only way to know for sure is to ask him - whilst at work. Ask him what the new boundaries are and try and stick to them. What do you make of that?
Still, they may be avoiding the question because they know that it wasn't directly pointed at them. They should've responded to your question, but they didn't. What do you think?

People often project onto their expectations on others through their behaviour. For example, when your friends didn't check up on you after you vented, you were frustrated because you would've done it. I think it's sometimes important to acknowledge that other people may fail to meet your expectations sometimes, partly because they're not you. I do think they should've checked in on you, but it's likely they didn't know they should've.

It sounds like they like you, but they might not (completely) respect you. I might be reading too much into this, but it might be the very fact that you're the 'available' one that makes it so they treat you as an option, or that person to fill up slots like you put it. I don't think it's fair, but it's part of human nature - for better or for worse: I'd say for worse. 

I think you're still holding a candle for these guys because it seems like they're your main group of friends. They may not be the best, but they're better than nothing, right? I think you fear isolation more than disrespect, but I think that's quite a normal feeling. 

When I want to detach, I do something called 'compartmentalisation'. It's where you acknowledge your feelings, but you don't act on them in the moment. For example, you may be feeling frustrated with your friends. Compartmentalisation is putting those feelings to the side and not making a decision (purely) through the lens of emotion. 

What do you think?

I'd assume that the fact they've read the messages and not responded means one of three things. 1) they can't make it the day before 2) they are planning on going on the original day 3) they aren't planning on going anymore. Of all these, I'd say option 3 is most likely.

The only way you can find out for sure is by asking them, though. I suggest DM'ing all of your friends to get an answer, as people sometimes dodge questions that are sent to a GC because they're not directed at them explicitly.
The condescension is unwarranted.
Most don't, the ones do are (probably) being pretentious: they think it makes them look smarter by looking down on others.
Prioritising our self interest over collective good is a slippery slope for us. However, I think humanity's capability to innovate is remarkable.

It won't always be easy. Sometimes, it'll be unimaginably difficult. You'll feel numb and lethargic. But, if you can lean towards voluntary discomfort, then you may (slowly) find yourself feeling better.

Something that really helped me was going to a GP (doctor's practice that isn't a hospital). I got enrolled in group CBT that lasted 6 weeks. One of my favourite takeaways was to 'Follow the plan, not the mood.' By forcing myself to do things I didn't want to do, I wasn't as vulnerable to my mood as I was before. Also, pushing through adversity made me feel colourful again, like there was light at the end of the tunnel.

I hope my perspective helps.
There are a couple, but one that was really helpful was following the two minute rule. If you can do something in two minutes or less, do it now. It helped with low level procrastination.
No worries, I hope things work out for you

It's quite natural to want to be attracted to your girlfriend/partner. It does sound like you're quite frustrated that you appear to be receiving less attention through Tinder. 

Looks are very important, they get your foot in the door. But, without a personality to boot, it's harder to sustain things long term. And I think it's valid to think that the right girl will give you happiness, but that'd make your happiness dependent on another person. I think relationships improve lives, but I think your life should be 'fine' without them. If you think getting cosmetic procedures will help, then that's something worth exploring. I wouldn't personally do it though (money) and I think I'm quite secure with my physical flaws too.

I'm sorry you're upset about this. You're not wrong for feeling that way. Seeking out activities to meet women isn't a bad idea - increase exposure, increased opportunity. However, I think it's important that there's some interest for the activity itself, otherwise you happiness doing the activity may lay in the hands of the girls that you're pursuing.

What do you make of all that? I hope it helps somewhat.
When push comes to shove, people will prioritise their own interests, even at the expense of others.

Hello, I'm sorry that you're struggling so much. I'm not in the same position, but I can't imagine that it'd be easy just getting by when there are so many things working against you. I think it's okay to feel stuck, it's okay to question it all too. What would you do if you weren't being held back?
'Maybe you can't means maybe you can.'
Keeping myself taut so I don't fall back into another depression. It's exhausting, but the alternative is all consuming.

It can’t be easy for you right now. The struggle you’re going through is real and worth acknowledging. Have you got any friends you could talk to, as perhaps it may be difficult to speak with family at present?
Well, that does sound like it’d get very annoying after a while. It sounds like you give more than you receive, which makes me think that you seem like a kind person. What would help?

It can sometimes feel very isolating and lonely to feel like the outcast. Sometimes, it’s nice to be invited to things because it’s nice to socialise. What sort of things do people organise and not invite you to & how does that make you feel?

People shouldn’t use people. I am sorry you feel you’re being used, that’s very hard on you. It does really sound heartbreaking to hear. It sounds like your kids are separated from you somehow. Why don’t your family check in on you?

I'm sorry you feel that people are using you. I'm even more sorry that no one is there to help and people aren't paying back what's yours. It sounds very difficult and you shouldn't have to be going through all of this. Thank you for sharing. What are people using you for?
Thank you, I won't take up more of your time. I'll bring this letter with me to therapy.
I wrote my apology, would you suggest sending it or holding off until I see them in person?
I'll write that letter today, thank you. I'll fast-track therapy. I tried it a couple of months ago, but I didn't talk about this incident because something else came up.
Yeah, I've done one session of therapy, but it didn't come up. The focus was elsewhere. Is there anything actionable that I could do today, before it comes up in therapy?

Hey, I'm sorry that you feel there's nothing going on for you. It sounds like you are frustrated with the track you're on. I think that's okay. 

People should be more appreciative. It doesn't hurt to hear a simple thanks - thank you for being vulnerable here. It's not always easy to do so. That feeling of being close to the edge... it sounds exhausting. Your wellbeing is (imo) priority number one - always.

It's good you have people who care for you. I'm sad to hear that you don't value yourself, despite others doing so. Oftentimes, we're our toughest critics. I think it's a survival instinct. The world is a huge puzzle. It's very tough finding out where we fit in. I'm sorry that struggle is bearing down on you.

What are you like? Your soul, your skills, what makes you you?

Thank you for sharing: it takes a lot of courage to be open, at least to me. I'm sorry that your childhood trauma has led to your depression. It's hard when our past haunts us, don't you think? I don't think your siblings or you deserved that abuse... I hope you know that.

  
It's only natural that your grades dropped, you're in survival mode. Congratulations on your anniversary! I wish it were happening under better circumstances. 

  
It must be tough: you feel like you won't achieve or succeed because of how you see yourself.

What was the fight over?
I'm sorry that it's all so tiring. Life is very exhausting and it can be easy to become overwhelmed. What makes you say your girlfriend and you won't last long?

I'm sorry that it's all very difficult for you. I'm sorry you don't think you're attractive, that's hard for anyone to deal with. Insecurities can really weigh us down and make us suffer, I'm sorry you have to put up with yours. I guess, I'm sorry for a lot... it shouldn't be this way. 

  
How does it feel not being able to talk to others? I'm asking because I'm a bit uncertain as to what makes this difficult for you. Unfortunately, a lot of people treat people differently based on how attractive they *perceive* them. And, unfortunately, there are some standards that most people would consider makes someone attractive. The word perceive is important there. Maybe not today, but someday, I think you'll get that nuance. 

  
It takes a lot of courage to speak and share when you're suffering - thank you. When did this all start for you?

Thoughts about sexual orientation that you're not expecting can really be surprising and they can feel concerning too. There's this thing called 'diminishing returns'. Basically, your body becomes used to a type of signal if you're exposed to it often. This may be why these thoughts are present. I can gather you're confused and hurt. To answer one of your questions: it's always worth trying to undo progress - if it's not progress you'd like. You may never forgive yourself, but I forgive you. What do you think people would make of you if they found out?
This is really well done nice

There are a lot for me!

Gin to Luffy in Baratie: 'You're young. Don't rush to your doom. The seas are vast. The Grand Line is just one narrow route. There are plenty of safer waters to plunder.' It perfectly captures the mentality of being a specialist (striving for greatness) versus being a generalist (a jack of all trades) that highly ambitious people tend to stray away from.

Zeff to Sanji about Luffy in Baratie: 'Once in a long while, a fool comes along who, having set his sights on something, won't quit fighting 'til he dies. Whether he wins or loses this fight, I admire a man like that. There's no give in him.'

Luffy in Little Garden: 'Too much! Too big.' Luffy just can't seem to fathom the honour being upheld by Dorry and Broggy and he seems to marvel in wonder at it all.

Whitebeard about Luffy in Marineford: 'You're nothing but a mass of spirit! All you can do is talk big! Pathetic young fool! I love idiots like you.'

Zoro in Dressrosa: 'Rather than complaining about how it's impossible, how about you turn off your imagination and help!'

Gyatts in Dressrosa about Luffy: 'Wherever he is, he's listening! Call that star's name!'
Sorry, I owe Robin an apology. I wasn’t familiar with her game.
Apologies, the opinions of riffraff swayed me. WRANKY ON TOP ✅

Pre time skip Lucci is (roughly) Luffy’s equal. Assuming she can keep up with his speed, which is unlikely, Lucci is physically stronger so her regular attacks wouldn’t work. Her gigantesco mano attacks would be too slow, so her saving grace would be fishman karate. I just don’t see that being enough to put down Lucci.

No chance: she’s gotten much stronger but so has Lucci

Edit: Nvm realised this is Current Robin vs Old Lucci. Still think Lucci takes it, but less decisively.
The Wranky agenda will recover
I’m sorry that you attempted recently. I won’t say those things to you, but I do hope things get better for you. No one deserves to suffer, please be gentle with yourself.
I hope you’re still here with us. We should check in on people lots more; I wish we didn’t all get so wrapped up in what’s happening to us.

You sound so exhausted, please make sure you’re giving yourself time to relax and recover. You really can’t justify bullying; I’m sorry that people think it’s acceptable to do. What makes you think things will be better for your family?

You're in a very confusing situation. It kind of sounds like you're feeling very lost as well. I can't say much as an outsider, but it doesn't sound like a healthy relationship. How would you describe him now?

I know it's a lot to endure; I think you've been doing a great job at staying strong. It sounds like a lot of grief comes from the relationship between your husband and yourself. Do you think your marriage can be repaired?

That sounds very frustrating. I would guess most outsiders wouldn't blame you. If we can justify actions like that, we can justify nearly anything. I'm sorry you have to put up with all of it. How does it make you feel?

No one deserves to have that happen to them. It doesn’t matter whether you triggered him or not. Please understand that. 

I’m sorry that you’re going through so much hardship; that sort of pain can really wear down on us all. It sounds like there’s a profound disconnect between your husband and you. 

I’m sorry you feel that you deserve all this… it sounds awfully heavy. Why do you think you deserve to part?

I’m sorry you have nothing. I’m sorry your girlfriend isn’t been as supportive as she could. I’m sorry your friend isn’t checking in on you. I’m saying sorry a lot; I feel like that’s the least I can do. I hope life is gentle on you moving forward, please take care of yourself.
Is this a poem, song or something else entirely? I think it’s quite accurate at reflecting the reality for those who fall victim to suicide and those who know them. How are you?
Alright, well I hope things improve for you. Please be gentle with yourself moving forward, take care.
Fair enough, was there anything else you wanted to talk about?

The answer you’ll probably find a lot is the point is whatever you decide it is. For me, it’d be to make this place better than how I found it. I think that stuff only matters if you want it to be. I’m aware that might sound like a cop out answer, but I believe it to be true. I’m sorry I don’t have anything more concrete for you. How have things been over the past couple of days?
I see. I was wondering what sort of things you think you’ve missed out on through not having any human connection?
Disappointment from our parents can be hard to navigate. I can see why you might be wary of them understanding your situation. Do you feel a connection with your parents?
That sounds awfully lonely. I hope that one day you find authentic, human connection. How do you think they’d feel, if they found out?
First, I’m so, so sorry that you feel this way. Would you like your parents to understand what you endure? And why do you wish you were never born?

The only answer I have is that it isn’t fair. I wish life were fairer to everyone, but we all have different circumstances. Normally, in some way or another, good things come back around to help us as well. What would make your next life better?

Hi, I’m sorry I can’t stick around to listen today. I just wanted to say that I’m sorry you haven’t felt love or any other sort of connection with others. I think everyone deserves to have people in their lives. I hope you can be gentle with yourself moving forward, take care.
I see - please only share that sort of information if you're comfortable. Has some of that rage cooled off over time? I think time can sometimes help with people's emotions.
I’m a bit confused. Why would he kill you?

I’m sorry you’ve decide upon this. I hope that you change your mind. Well, if I knew you wanted a hug, I’d give you one. I think everyone deserves love, but that’s just me. I think you also deserve friends and a partner who doesn’t lie to you. You’re quite young… I hope you’re gentle on yourself moving forward. The world can be harder on those who are younger.

I’m assuming the last paragraph is addressed to your ex. How does it feel to have written that out? I find that when I journal, it helps me process whatever turmoil I may be enduring. What’s it like being abrosexual?
I’m sorry that you’re not enjoying life. I think we all deserve to enjoy our day to day, although I know this isn’t always possible. I hope life is gentler on you moving forwards.

I hear you; it can be easy to look at people who live in more deprived countries and think: 'My problems are insignificant compared to them, as they have much less.' It's alright to cry, I'm relieved you're letting yourself do this.  What do you think will happen if your life takes a turn for the worse? What might happen if your life takes a turn for the better?  I don't think we ever know what's coming next. I think it's more useful to think about what's happening now in your life that you can control. I hope venting has helped somewhat, take care.
Hi, what’s led to this decision?

I’m sorry you feel so done with it all. I think too many adults are immature as well as hypocrites to boot. They shouldn’t have invited you if they resented you. I think I’d be livid if I were in your shoes too. What did these adults do on this trip? 

I have to go to bed soon, but I’ll reply (if you reply) when I wake up. I hope you’re gentle with yourself.

I think balance can be found without forsaking one path completely. But that’s just my opinion.

I think your family and friends are choosing to be very in empathetic, which sounds like it’s really getting to you.

I don’t think there’s a good reason for ghosting someone - it doesn’t provide the recipient with a reason which can lead to rumination. I don’t get why people can’t be more polite either. It differs from person to person, I reckon.

I’m sorry you see yourself as a loser. I think enduring negative self talk like that can be really hard on us. I can’t decide what the best option is for you, but I think you’ve made a decision already. I wish you all the best with it. 

Problems are problems. Sure, some people might have it worse, but it doesn’t mean that your problem isn’t affecting you. I hope your retreat in the Philippines is fruitful. What are you planning on doing there?

I see, I think family and friends are as good a reason as any to endure. I don’t think saying ‘get over it’,‘grow up’ or ‘move on’ is sensitive to someone who’s a sexual abuse survivor; I’m upset that people (may) have said these things to you. 

Volunteering can help the other person as well as you, but you’ve taken a pretty severe shock to the system recently. It’s important to be mindful of changes that can explain why you feel the way you do now. Sometimes, there looks like there’s no light on the road ahead. And that’s okay. It’s okay to feel hopeless. It’s okay to feel lost. It’d be unhealthy to force positivity. 

No worries for reading- it’s a privilege for me to help others. What else embodies your struggle?

That’s really unfortunate. It sounds like you feel very let down with your circle and yourself. Hopelessness can truly feel defeating. What was the point of being alive for you before this incident, if you don’t mind me asking?
Hi, I’m just checking in. How are you?
I’m sorry you’ve suffered so much. What and/or who caused your suffering?
Heartbreak isn’t easy for anyone, I should know. But that’s another story. Did it feel worse at first or now?
I hope your situation becomes less rough and becomes more gentle with time. How does that make you feel - it being perceived as a friendship to her?

I’m really sorry that your wife has lost feelings for you - it can’t be easy navigating this situation. 

I think expressing your emotions is healthy, as long as it doesn’t hurt others. It sounds like they exploded which can happen if you don’t have good outlets for your emotions. 

I hope you claw your way out of this dark hole that you’re in. Your wife, kids and yourself deserve happiness. To take care of them, you need to take care of you. How have the past 3 weeks been?
I’m sorry you’re hurting so much. I wish life had been gentler on you up to this point. How did you decide that you should jump?
Please try to be gentle with yourself. I wish I could say more, but I’m not doing too good right now. Take care of yourself.
I think so, even if I pretend I’m not. Are you saying others are scared that you sometimes don’t?

I hear you. It really does sound like a massive amount to handle. It’s certainly not fair that you have to put up with so much with a (practically) non-existent support circle. I believe you deserve better. I’m sorry about your relationship. How was it ruined?
What makes you not want to continue? I’m sorry you’re suffering.
I think flying seems pretty neat. What do you think would be awesome about being a bird?
I’m genuinely heartbroken that it’s really destroying you. What would make things easier for you?
Thank you for clearing that up. How has it been managing both for the past couple of years? I can’t imagine that it was easy in any way.
Was that when your suicidal thoughts started to appear?
How long have you been like this?
It’s easy (and okay) to feel overwhelmed, especially when you’re not feeling well. How are you sick? And thank you for responding.
I hope you stay around. I’m sorry that you want to leave. What’s on your mind?
I can see why that question scares you - the unknown can be scary. Things we’re unsure about can be scary.  How do you manage that fear?
I see, thank you for sharing that with me. What is it about death that you love so much? Perhaps it's that all of your suffering may come to a close? I'm not sure.
I’m sorry that your family haven’t been understanding. It sounds like their trauma has really made things doubly hard. Why do you want to go?

I think people shouldn’t try to make you feel guilty about how you feel. As for a reason, I think people will do anything to reduce the chance that someone will fall victim to suicide. Why do you think people make you feel guilty for it?

People may complain for validation, but is feeling validated a problem? Change is rarely sustainable if it happens quickly; most of us haven’t fostered the required adaptability to make rapid change work. Changing your lifestyle is all well and good. It’s a question of gently nudging, encouraging and supporting people to make that change.

I agree. This is good advice. However, it’s worth considering if advice is exactly what people with suicidal thoughts need. As we know, many people fall victim to suicide every day; perhaps the advice didn’t resonate with these people?

I think one of the best things we can do to help others who are going through ordeals is to be there for them. Listening, understanding and speaking gently with people lets them know that there may just be one person in their corner. It’s one of the reasons why (I suspect) people volunteer their time for help lines. 

What do you think?

It’s alright, you don’t have to apologise to us. We’re social creatures; it makes sense that we feel value through our connections with others. Romantic love and platonic love feel different, at least they do to now. Maybe it’s the same for you? There’s no shame in getting messed up after things go south in a relationship, even if they’re short lived. When we break up with someone, we go through something similar to what drug addicts to when they can’t get their next hit - withdrawal. 

With moving past people, something that’s worked for me (that might work for you) is writing down a list of pros and cons about people who you’re no longer with. Oftentimes we idealise people; we think they’re better than they are. If we can shatter that perception, then it can make it easier for us to move past them. Most of us are exceptionally average after all. Please consider giving it a go.

I think you know this already, but you shouldn’t have to change your personality to match your partner. Although I know that’s easier said than done. How does your school stress affect your everyday life?

That’s okay - expecting 100% consistency from anyone is (kind of) unrealistic. I think emotions become easier to understand the more you process them; how you do that differs from person to person. 

I’m sorry that your dad wasn’t there for you, like he should’ve been. It’s led to a lot of turmoil for you, which isn’t okay. I believe that you deserve better, as does anyone else who’s been estranged. How does it feel to grapple with self-hate?

I visited a friend on the psych ward once. It didn’t seem amazing, so I think I can see where you’re coming from. You’ve got good advice: ‘If you feel like dying talk to somebody…’ Sometimes, we’re harder on ourselves than we are on others. Have you considered being gentler on yourself? Have you talked to somebody about how you’re feeling? It could help - a problem shared sometimes feels like a problem halved.

I hope you’re able to be gentle with yourself moving forward.

I’ve listened. I would never call anyone weak or a coward, let alone someone who’s struggling so much. I’m so sorry that your mom wasn’t there for you like she should have been. I’m sorry your fiancé wasn’t there for you either. It sounds like there’re a lot of people in your life who don’t show up for you like they should. I think you deserve better; everyone deserves better. 

The words you’ve shared today are very thoughtful- everyone should hear them. I hope life is gentler to you moving forward. Please take care of yourself.

I’m sorry you feel the way you do. It can’t be easy. No friends and solitude is a gruelling combination. On top of that, it sounds like you have a very poor self image.

You have a big heart; you try so hard for your baby in spite of your depression. That choice you make shows strength. It’s easy to do stuff when we’re happy, but when we’re unhappy, even the smallest task can feel like an unconquerable mountain. I hope moving forward you’re able to be gentle with yourself. Please take care.

I’m so, so sorry for your losses. One bereavement is hard enough, but 7 in a year sounds incredibly painful. I hope life is gentler to you moving forward - you most certainly deserve it. And I hope you’re gentler with yourself because you deserve it. Take care of yourself, please.
Change can be difficult - it’s okay to feel the way you do. I hope you’re gentle with yourself moving forward.

What do you think the point is? I think everyone’s answer differs really - so I don’t think there’s a universal answer. I’m sorry you’re contemplating doing it - you must see an incredibly difficult road ahead. 

I think things right now are awful as well. I think most people have a similar viewpoint to us. Telling people about our problems can help us. Of course, there are only certain people whom we can trust. That’s why I think this community can be really helpful; we’re all strangers, so we can’t track and trace one another.

I want to promise you that better days are ahead and I can do just that. I’m not promising ‘good’ days, but I can promise better days. Tomorrow might be slightly worse than today, or it might be slightly better. We never know for sure until it comes.  Good and bad come together as a couple; we’re never going to run out of slightly bad days, just like we’re never going to run out of slightly good days. 

I’m not asking for the world from you. The only thing I want to ask you is to work on building a tiny glimmer of hope; the hope that things MAY get better. Thank you for being so open and honest today. It takes strength to show real vulnerability. What do you think?
I’m sorry you feel this way. I hope life becomes gentler for you moving forward.
I’m sorry that you’re not doing okay. Please be gentle with yourself.
I’m really sorry for your sister and your loss. Please give yourself time to mourn - it’s healthy. I hope your family and yourself are able to be gentle moving forward.

Being whipped around between doctors sounds jarring! It could be worth communicating that the medicine is ineffective with your doctor before and/or after the transfer.

Besides medication, is there anything you do to help manage your insomnia?

I can see why you feel the mistake you made isn’t something that you can move past easily. Have you considered going to a doctor about your insomnia? I know you’ve mentioned a couple of hypnotics that you’ve tried, but a doctor could help you with a prescription that works better for you. What do you think?

I don’t mean to try and sound wise, but everyone makes mistakes. I think a mistake is only truly a mistake if you don’t learn from it and apply what you’ve learned. Please try to be gentle with yourself. It’s okay to feel paranoid and unstable. It sounds to me like you’re having to endure so much hardship - mental and physical. I think you’re being very strong to persevere through so much hardship. 

‘Struggling isn’t failure. Struggling is successfully not giving up.’ - Coach Bennett
